title: Samaya Sterling Beats Claude Fable 5.1 at 11x Lower Cost

body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Samaya AI launched Sterling, a 3B-active parameter finance research model that achieves 58.9% accuracy on the FrontierFinance benchmark.
- Sterling costs $0.61 per question, delivering 11x cost savings compared to Claude Fable 5.1's $6.89 while outperforming it by 3 percentage points.
- Built on post-trained Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, Sterling targets financial research agents requiring accurate, cost-efficient reasoning at scale.


Samaya AI has released Sterling, a 3B-active parameter model purpose-built for financial research agents. Officially launched on October 30, 2026, Sterling achieves 58.9% accuracy on the FrontierFinance benchmark at a cost of $0.61 per question, outperforming Claude Fable 5.1's 55.9% accuracy at $6.89 per question. The result represents an 11x cost reduction while delivering superior performance on domain-specific financial reasoning tasks.


## Architecture and Post-Training Approach


Sterling is a post-trained variant of Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a small-footprint language model optimized for fast inference. Samaya AI applied domain-specific fine-tuning using curated financial datasets, regulatory filings, earnings transcripts, and market research documents. The post-training pipeline included supervised instruction tuning on financial question-answer pairs and reinforcement learning from human feedback provided by certified financial analysts.


The 3B-active parameter architecture enables Sterling to run efficiently on consumer-grade GPUs and edge devices, reducing infrastructure overhead for enterprises deploying financial research agents at scale. Samaya reports sub-200ms latency for typical financial queries when deployed on an NVIDIA L4 GPU.


## FrontierFinance Benchmark Performance


FrontierFinance is a multi-task benchmark evaluating language models on financial statement analysis, regulatory compliance interpretation, equity research, credit risk assessment, and macroeconomic forecasting. Sterling's 58.9% score surpasses Claude Fable 5.1's 55.9% and positions it among the top-performing models under 10B parameters.


- Financial statement analysis: 62.3% accuracy (Claude Fable 5.1: 58.7%)
- Regulatory compliance: 56.1% accuracy (Claude Fable 5.1: 54.2%)
- Credit risk assessment: 60.4% accuracy (Claude Fable 5.1: 55.1%)


The benchmark results suggest that domain-specific post-training on smaller models can outperform larger general-purpose models on vertical tasks, particularly when cost per inference is a constraint.


## Cost Efficiency and Deployment Economics


Sterling's $0.61 per question cost is calculated based on the model's token consumption and Samaya's published API pricing of $0.08 per million input tokens and $0.24 per million output tokens. Claude Fable 5.1's $6.89 per question reflects Anthropic's enterprise API rates for extended-context financial queries.


For financial services firms processing thousands of research queries daily, the 11x cost differential translates to significant operational savings. A hedge fund running 10,000 queries per day would spend approximately $6,100 per day with Sterling versus $68,900 with Claude Fable 5.1, an annual difference exceeding $22 million.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially released on October 30, 2026, Sterling is available via Samaya AI's API and as a self-hosted deployment option for enterprise customers. The company offers tiered pricing: a pay-per-query API at standard rates, a volume-discounted plan for firms processing over 1 million queries per month, and an on-premises license for regulated institutions requiring air-gapped deployments.


Samaya has published model weights under a research license for academic institutions and released an open-source evaluation harness for FrontierFinance to encourage reproducible benchmarking in the financial AI community.


## What This Means


Sterling demonstrates that specialized small models can outperform larger general-purpose systems in vertical domains when post-training is applied rigorously. For financial services firms balancing accuracy, cost, and regulatory compliance, Sterling offers a viable alternative to frontier models at a fraction of the operational expense. The release also underscores a broader industry trend: as pre-trained base models mature, domain-specific fine-tuning and efficient architectures are becoming competitive advantages in enterprise AI adoption.
